sections.html:
Polk County lies in western Oregon, just west of Salem. Marion County lies across the Willamette on the east, and the valley fills the eastern half of Polk. The county seat is Dallas. Other cities include Independence, Monmouth, Falls City and part of Willamina, and West Salem, on the county's side of the river, belongs to the City of Salem.

Roughly 90,037 people lived here in mid-2025, in 36,026 housing units, 64.7% of them owner-occupied. A typical owner-occupied home was worth $454,700 for 2020 to 2024. Forest covers roughly the western two-thirds, so sellers here may hold a valley lot near Salem or a timber parcel toward the Coast Range. Use that figure loosely, since a farm outside Rickreall and a Monmouth house can land far from it.

The job is shared. Value is the Assessor's call. The Tax and Finance Office, 850 Main Street, Dallas, Oregon 97338, sends bills and takes payments. For an appeal, get forms from the County Clerk and file with the Property Value Appeals Board.

Late October brings the statements. They come in four kinds (real, personal, manufactured structure and utility), each for the July 1 to June 30 tax year. A note in the information section shows when a mortgage company requested the bill. Online, the county offers an account lookup and a contact form.

DateWhat happens
January 1Valuation date for real market value
February 14Second payment due on the three-payment plan
March 15Property returns due
April 1Last day to apply for exemptions and the farm and forest deferral
April 15Senior deferral application deadline; appeals board adjourns
May 15Third payment due; unpaid real property tax becomes delinquent
October 25Last day to mail tax statements; appeal filing opens
November 15First payment due
December 31Last day to file an appeal; late exemption applications accepted with a penalty

Weekend and holiday dates roll to the next business day. If you mail anything, ask the post office for a hand-stamped postmark dated no later than the deadline.

Settle the year in November and take 3% off. Send two-thirds and take 2% off that payment. Three equal installments get no discount.

Payment channels: the Tax Office counter, a drop box in the courthouse parking lot, mail, online and phone. Fees apply online and by phone. Banks around town have stopped accepting property tax.

At a sale, the title or escrow company checks the account, then splits the current year between you and the buyer on the settlement statement. Request the status early. An installment you forgot can surface as an unwelcome payoff line.

Tax is levied on assessed value, whichever is lower of real market value and maximum assessed value. The maximum climbs 3% a year at most, unless there is new construction, a major remodel, rezoning or a new lot.

Measure 5 sets its own ceilings tied to real market value: $5 per $1,000 for education and $10 per $1,000 for general government. Voter-approved bonds usually sit outside them, and local option levies are trimmed first when a category goes over.

So an owner of many years can pay far less than someone who just bought a similar home. And a market value cut will not always cut the tax if assessed value was already lower.

Real property tax is delinquent after May 15, and ORS 312.010 allows foreclosure three years after that delinquency date.

  • By about July 16 the Tax Collector drafts the foreclosure list and mails owners of record a notice, first-class and certified.
  • Around August 16 the Polk County Itemizer-Observer prints the list, the county seeks judgment, and a 5% penalty goes on.
  • An owner may answer in Circuit Court within 30 days of publication.
  • Judgment sells the property to the county and starts a two-year redemption period.
  • Redeeming takes the back taxes and interest, the 5% penalty, 9% annual interest from judgment and a fee of at least $50, all at once. No partial payments.

An unredeemed property goes to the county free of liens, apart from municipal local improvement assessments. Parcels paid off before publication are dropped, so a seller who is behind may want to close a sale before then and pay from the proceeds.

The petition goes to the Property Value Appeals Board and is due December 31, rolling to the next business day on a weekend or holiday. The board sits starting the first Monday in February and may continue to April 15.

The argument is about real market value on January 1. Most owners bring a sale price, an appraisal or comparable sales from around then, so collect them before filing. A board ruling can be taken next to the Oregon Tax Court.

Selling soon? Check with the title company on whether a pending appeal changes the closing numbers.

Start with the newest statement and see which installments are settled. Anything open? Request a payoff figure from the Tax Office, and let the title company know about an appeal underway. If you hold timber or farm land, check the April 1 deadline for the farm and forest deferral, and for any exemption you may be missing. Cash offers skip the lender's appraisal, a plus for a hillside parcel or an older home with put-off repairs.

sections.h2: Timing a Polk County sale around the tax calendar
sections.html: Use the calendar when choosing a listing date. A closing just ahead of November 15 means the first installment is nearly due, and a spring closing bumps against the April 1 exemption deadline and the May 15 third payment. Sellers with timber or farm acreage should remember the April 1 deferral date and the April 15 senior deferral deadline, since missing them means waiting a full year. Whatever the date, agree with the buyer on paper who covers each installment, so the settlement statement matches your expectations.

sections.h2: Dallas, Monmouth, Independence and Falls City
sections.html:
The four cities differ in size and setting.

  • Dallas: 16,854 residents in 2020, along Rickreall Creek about 15 miles west of Salem. About 47.8 inches of precipitation fall in a year.
  • Monmouth: 11,110 residents in 2020, about 12 miles west of Salem on Oregon Route 99W, home to Western Oregon University.
  • Independence: 9,828 residents in 2020, on the west bank of the Willamette River. A December 1861 flood wiped out its commercial district and farms.
  • Falls City: 1,051 residents in 2020, in the Coast Range hills with the Little Luckiamute River through its center.

Homes close to the Willamette or a creek should get a flood-risk review before listing. After wet winters, buyers go straight to roofs, gutters and crawl space moisture.

faqs.q: Which office collects Polk County property tax?
faqs.a: The Tax and Finance Office, 850 Main Street in Dallas. Values come from the Assessor.

faqs.q: When are Polk County property taxes due?
faqs.a: Payments come due November 15, February 15 and May 15, moving ahead to a business day if needed. Paying everything in November earns 3% off.

faqs.q: When must a Polk County appeal be filed?
faqs.a: By December 31 (next business day if that is a weekend or holiday). The board hears cases from the first Monday in February to April 15.

faqs.q: How far behind can I fall before foreclosure?
faqs.a: Three years after the delinquency date, with taxes unpaid after May 15 counting as delinquent. Judgment is followed by two years to redeem.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Polk County house with unpaid property tax?
faqs.a: Yes. The title company usually pays the tax and interest from your proceeds at the closing table, once you have a payoff figure in hand.
